description: r.jina.ai used without an API key (line 22) is rate-limited by Jina (keyless tier is a low requests-per-minute cap; keyed tier is far higher). The product is meant to be served behind an x402 paywall where buyers pay and call it repeatedly; under any concurrency or sustained traffic the keyless reads will return 429, every source in a request can fail, and the run exits 1 at line 43 ('all source reads failed'). This is a hidden reliability/cost cliff: the $0/no-key invariant is satisfied only at near-zero volume, exactly the volume a paid product is not operated at. The spec's $0 claim should explicitly acknowledge the keyless throughput ceiling, or the impl should add backoff/fallback, or the spec should accept that scaling requires a Jina key (which would itself collide with R5).
